report_title: Rocket Kitten (Group 41 / Operation Woolen-Goldfish / Thamar Reservoir / Ajax-adjacent) Actor Intelligence Pack — Stage-1 CTI Extraction
source: Check Point 'Rocket Kitten: A Campaign With 9 Lives' (2015-11, https://blog.checkpoint.com/research/rocket-kitten-a-campaign-with-9-lives/ ; report PDF https://blog.checkpoint.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/rocket-kitten-report.pdf); Trend Micro 'Operation Woolen-GoldFish: When Kittens Go Phishing' (2015-03, https://documents.trendmicro.com/assets/wp/wp-operation-woolen-goldfish.pdf); Trend Micro 'The Spy Kittens Are Back: Rocket Kitten 2' (2015-09, https://documents.trendmicro.com/assets/wp/wp-the-spy-kittens-are-back.pdf); ClearSky 'Thamar Reservoir' (2015-06, https://www.clearskysec.com/thamar-reservoir/ , PDF https://www.clearskysec.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Thamar-Reservoir-public1.pdf); MITRE ATT&CK Group 'Ajax Security Team' G0130 (Rocket Kitten cluster, https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0130/)

actor.name: Rocket Kitten
aliases: Ajax Security Team (MITRE G0130 cluster alias)
related_clusters: Charming Kitten (distinct but frequently confused Iran-nexus espionage cluster; separate actor)
Ajax Security Team / Flying Kitten / Operation Saffron Rose (MITRE folds Rocket Kitten and these into G0130; infrastructure/persona overlap, honestly noted as adjacent not identical)
Thamar Reservoir (ClearSky-tracked campaign attributed to this group)
actor.attribution: Iran-nexus cyber-espionage group, assessed as aligned with / operating on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Attribution rests on convergence of: Farsi-language artifacts and operator handles (Wool3n.H4t / 'Masoud_pk', 'Yaser'), targeting sets of clear Iranian state interest (Israeli defense and academia, Saudi Arabia, and Iranian dissidents/journalists/human-rights activists at home and in diaspora), Iranian hosting/registration pivots (an inactive Iran-hosted blog for Wool3n.H4t; use of the free Iranian AV-scanning service av.zerodays.ir to pre-test samples), and re-use of the same custom GHOLE/CWoolger tooling and personas across campaigns. MITRE tracks the cluster under Ajax Security Team (G0130). Overlaps with Flying Kitten / Operation Saffron Rose are acknowledged honestly as adjacent (shared code/persona lineage), and Rocket Kitten is DISTINCT from Charming Kitten despite frequent conflation. Sophistication is moderate: mature enough targeting/social-engineering but amateur tooling (macro delivery, plaintext-then-weakly-encrypted FTP credentials, leaked debug PDB paths).

key_campaigns.name: Operation Woolen-GoldFish / The GHOLE Campaign
key_campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing of Israeli and European targets with malicious Microsoft Office (Excel/PowerPoint) attachments and OneDrive-hosted decoys. Opening the Office file and enabling a VBA macro drops and executes a GHOLE backdoor DLL (a modified Core Impact agent) that beacons over HTTP to a hard-coded C2 IP (e.g. 83.170.33.60) using GET /index.php?c=&r=&u=&t= with a 256-bit key. A OneDrive link delivered 'Iran's Missiles Program.ppt.exe' (PowerPoint icon, double extension) which drops a benign decoy and silently installs the CWoolger (TSPY_WOOLERG) keylogger. Attribution artifacts include the operator handle Wool3n.H4t and PDB path C:\Users\Wool3n.H4t\...\CWoolger\Release\CWoolger.pdb.

key_campaigns.name: The Spy Kittens Are Back (Rocket Kitten 2)
key_campaigns.summary: Continued Middle East espionage. New TSPY_WOOLERG keylogger variants (debug strings 'D:\Yaser Logers\...') add a basic encryption layer over the previously plaintext hard-coded FTP credentials and exfiltrate keystroke logs via FTP to 107.6.172.54/woolen/ (earlier 107.6.181.116). Heavy persona/social-engineering: fake Facebook profiles (e.g. 'mah.asf.xxx'), impersonation of a security researcher via a spoofed sender clearsky.cybersec.group@gmail.com, and a fake Trend Micro HouseCall installer (HousecallLauncher.exe) beaconing to 84.11.146.62.

key_campaigns.name: Thamar Reservoir
key_campaigns.summary: ClearSky-tracked campaign (named for target Thamar E. Gindin) using coordinated spear-phishing, fake-login credential-harvesting pages spoofing webmail/portal logins, and phone/email social-engineering with tailored fake identities against Middle East scholars, scientists, journalists and activists. Overlapping infrastructure and GHOLE malware tie it to Rocket Kitten.

key_campaigns.name: Rocket Kitten: A Campaign With 9 Lives (operational database exposure)
key_campaigns.summary: Check Point/ClearSky obtained the group's target-management database, revealing ~1,600 targets: scholars, scientists, CEOs, ministry officials, education institutes, media/journalists and human-rights activists across the Middle East, Europe and the US. Confirmed persona-driven spear-phishing, phishing domains and a phishing server, and minimal tooling/domain changes even after public exposure.

malware: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
Fake Trend Micro HouseCall installer (HousecallLauncher.exe backdoor installer)
tooling_observed: Malicious Microsoft Office (Excel / PowerPoint) documents with VBA macros
Fake login / credential-harvesting web pages (webmail and portal spoofs)
Fake social-media profiles (Facebook) and webmail personas
Core Impact Pro (commercial pentest tool, modified into GHOLE)
av.zerodays.ir (free Iranian AV multiscanner, used to pre-test detection)

ttps.procedure_description: Actors research individual targets (names, roles, email addresses, phone numbers, professional interests) to craft highly tailored spear-phishing lures and fake identities; the recovered operational database held ~1,600 profiled targets.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — victim-side profiling and OSINT occur off-victim and are not endpoint-observable; intel/hunt candidate via targeted-user awareness and external exposure monitoring

ttps.procedure_description: Actors identify and prioritize target organizations of Iranian state interest — Israeli defense and academic institutions, ministries, research institutes, media outlets and human-rights NGOs — to focus espionage collection.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — organizational targeting research is off-victim; intel candidate only

ttps.procedure_description: Actors create fake social-media personas (e.g. Facebook profiles communicating in perfect Farsi/Hebrew) to build rapport with targets; when a profile is taken down they recreate it (e.g. 'mah.asf.xxx' where xxx is a random number). One fake profile even sent a friend request to a ClearSky researcher.
observed_tooling: Fake social-media profiles (Facebook) and webmail personas
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — actor-controlled social accounts are off-victim; brand/impersonation-monitoring and user-reporting candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Actors register webmail persona accounts to correspond with targets and send lures (e.g. a Yahoo account '[name]_asf@yahoo.com', and a Gmail sender clearsky.cybersec.group@gmail.com impersonating the ClearSky research group).
observed_tooling: Fake social-media profiles (Facebook) and webmail personas
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — attacker-controlled sender accounts are off-victim; inbound-mail sender/impersonation analytics apply at delivery time

ttps.procedure_description: Actors impersonate real, recognizable people (a known Israeli engineer, a defense-field figure) and are assessed to have compromised at least one such person's computer to steal genuine documents (identical file metadata) subsequently reused as authentic-looking lures against other Israeli targets.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — compromise/impersonation of a third party's identity and mailbox is off the defender's network; intel/hunt candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Actors register phishing/look-alike domains and operate a phishing server for credential-harvesting fake-login pages; the group made only minimal changes to these domains even after public exposure.
observed_tooling: Fake login / credential-harvesting web pages (webmail and portal spoofs)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via newly-registered/look-alike-domain monitoring

ttps.procedure_description: Actors abuse legitimate cloud/web services — notably Microsoft OneDrive to host malicious payloads — to bypass email attachment scanning, and used the free Iranian multiscanner av.zerodays.ir to pre-test their samples' detection.
observed_tooling: Microsoft OneDrive (payload hosting)
av.zerodays.ir (free Iranian AV multiscanner, used to pre-test detection)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — off-victim staging on third-party services; intel/hunt candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Actors upload malicious executables to cloud storage for delivery — e.g. an archive containing 'Iran's Missiles Program.ppt.exe' (PowerPoint icon, double extension) staged on a OneDrive link sent to targets.
observed_tooling: Microsoft OneDrive (payload hosting)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — payload staged on attacker-controlled cloud is off-victim until delivery; intel/hunt candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Actors developed the custom CWoolger keylogger (TSPY_WOOLERG); leaked PDB debug paths (C:\Users\Wool3n.H4t\...\CWoolger\Release\CWoolger.pdb and D:\Yaser Logers\...) tie authorship to the operator handles Wool3n.H4t and Yaser.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — malware development is off-victim; the compiled artifact's runtime behavior is where detection lands — intel candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Actors obtain and repurpose commercial/off-the-shelf tooling — the GHOLE backdoor is a modified Core Impact Pro pentest agent.
observed_tooling: Core Impact Pro (commercial pentest tool, modified into GHOLE)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — tool acquisition is off-endpoint; downstream deployment is where detection lands — intel candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Primary initial-access vector: tailored spear-phishing emails carrying malicious Microsoft Office attachments (Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint, or PDF decoys) themed to the target's professional interests; opening the file and enabling macros drops the GHOLE backdoor.
observed_tooling: Malicious Microsoft Office (Excel / PowerPoint) documents with VBA macros
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — inbound Office attachments with macros are inspectable at the mail gateway/sandbox; endpoint detection lands at the macro-execution stage rather than delivery

ttps.procedure_description: Actors send links (including OneDrive links) that lead to a malicious executable disguised with a PowerPoint icon ('Iran's Missiles Program.ppt.exe'), and links to fake-login credential-harvesting pages, storing payloads online to bypass email attachment detection.
observed_tooling: Microsoft OneDrive (payload hosting)
Fake login / credential-harvesting web pages (webmail and portal spoofs)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — outbound clicks to newly-seen cloud/look-alike URLs are detectable at proxy/mail-URL-rewrite, though attribution requires infrastructure context

ttps.procedure_description: Actors initiate contact and deliver lures via non-email services — fake Facebook profiles and social-media messaging — building trust in Farsi/Hebrew before delivering malicious files or links.
observed_tooling: Fake social-media profiles (Facebook) and webmail personas
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — third-party social-platform contact is off-victim and outside enterprise telemetry; user-awareness/hunt candidate

ttps.procedure_description: Compromise requires the user to open the Office attachment and enable the embedded macro (which drops/executes the GHOLE DLL), or to run the disguised '.ppt.exe' which drops a benign decoy while silently installing the CWoolger keylogger.
observed_tooling: Malicious Microsoft Office (Excel / PowerPoint) documents with VBA macros
GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — Office applications (winword/excel/powerpnt) spawning script/dropper child processes and writing a DLL/EXE, and execution of double-extension .ppt.exe, are high-fidelity endpoint signals via process-lineage and image-load telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: Targets are induced to click OneDrive/phishing links; in one analyzed case attackers replied in Hebrew to confirm an email's authenticity, convincing the target to proceed.
observed_tooling: Microsoft OneDrive (payload hosting)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — link-click to file-download followed by execution is reconstructable from proxy + endpoint telemetry, but the click itself blends with normal browsing

ttps.technique_name: Office Application Startup: Office Template Macros
ttps.procedure_description: Malicious Office documents embed VBA macros that, when enabled, drop the GHOLE backdoor DLL to disk and execute it; the delivery documents are detected as X2KM_DROPPR.
observed_tooling: Malicious Microsoft Office (Excel / PowerPoint) documents with VBA macros
X2KM_DROPPR (malicious macro Office-document dropper)
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — VBA macro execution that writes and launches a PE is detectable via Office macro-runtime (AMSI), VBA-project inspection and Office-spawns-child-process rules

ttps.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
ttps.procedure_description: Delivery uses VBA macros in Office files, and the CWoolger keylogger drops a VBScript 'wsc.vbs' in %TEMP% that installs its persistence mechanism.
observed_tooling: VBScript (wsc.vbs) persistence installer
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — creation/execution of wsc.vbs in %TEMP% via wscript/cscript and macro VBA activity are captured by script-block/AMSI and process-creation logging

ttps.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
ttps.procedure_description: The CWoolger keylogger copies itself to %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe, creates a 'woolger' mutex, and its wsc.vbs installs a Startup-folder shortcut named 'WinDefender' (using the Notepad icon) that launches the malware at logon.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
VBScript (wsc.vbs) persistence installer
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — a new Startup-folder shortcut named 'WinDefender' pointing to %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe (and the 'woolger' mutex) are actor-specific, high-fidelity persistence detections via file/registry and process telemetry

ttps.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
ttps.procedure_description: Persistence is implemented as a .lnk shortcut ('WinDefender', spoofing the Notepad icon) placed in the Startup folder that resolves to the keylogger binary in %TEMP%.
observed_tooling: VBScript (wsc.vbs) persistence installer
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — creation of a Startup .lnk whose target resides in %TEMP% is a rare, high-fidelity signal via file-creation and shortcut-target auditing

ttps.procedure_description: CWoolger enables keylogging via the SetWindowsHookExW API and records all keystrokes to %TEMP%\wlg.dat (later variants %TEMP%\AdobeARM.log / %TEMP%\AdobeARMM.log) in a '[Window Title] - [Application Name] ([Language])' + context format, using SetTimer to schedule uploads.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — creation/growth of %TEMP% log files named wlg.dat / AdobeARM.log / AdobeARMM.log by a non-Adobe process, plus SetWindowsHookExW keyboard hooks from an unsigned %TEMP% binary, are strong host detections

ttps.procedure_description: Actors operate fake-login / credential-harvesting web pages (spoofing webmail and institutional portal logins) linked from spear-phishing messages to capture target account credentials; a dedicated phishing server supported this.
observed_tooling: Fake login / credential-harvesting web pages (webmail and portal spoofs)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — the harvesting page is off-victim adversary infrastructure; hunt candidate via mail-URL/proxy telemetry to look-alike login domains and impossible-travel logons after credential theft

ttps.procedure_description: Fake login pages mimicking legitimate webmail/portal sign-in forms capture the credentials entered by targets, feeding the group's account-compromise objectives.
observed_tooling: Fake login / credential-harvesting web pages (webmail and portal spoofs)
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — credential capture occurs on attacker-hosted pages outside defender telemetry; hunt via post-theft anomalous-authentication analytics

ttps.procedure_description: The delivery executable uses a double extension and spoofed icon ('Iran's Missiles Program.ppt.exe' with a PowerPoint icon) to appear as a document, and the GHOLE DLL exports a benign-looking function named 'function' instead of the telltale 'gholee' to evade detection.
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — double-extension executables with document icons and PE files masquerading as .ppt are detectable via file-type/extension-mismatch and icon-resource heuristics, but need scanning coverage

ttps.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
ttps.procedure_description: Malware and its artifacts adopt legitimate-looking names to blend in: keylogger drops as NTUSER.dat{GUID}.exe and %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe, persists as 'WinDefender', logs to AdobeARM.log/AdobeARMM.log, and one installer masquerades as Trend Micro HouseCall (HousecallLauncher.exe).
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
Fake Trend Micro HouseCall installer (HousecallLauncher.exe backdoor installer)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — names mimicking system/AV/Adobe artifacts (NTUSER.dat*.exe, NTSuser.exe, WinDefender, AdobeARM*.log, HousecallLauncher.exe) in %TEMP%/startup are detectable via name/path/signer baselining

ttps.procedure_description: Later CWoolger variants add a basic encryption layer to hide the hard-coded FTP credentials (earlier versions stored them in clear text); GHOLE carries a 256-byte (2,048-bit) key used to obfuscate network communications.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — embedded high-entropy blobs/keys and encoded credential strings are detectable via static/entropy analysis, but require sample-level inspection

ttps.procedure_description: Some Rocket Kitten malware places its payload in memory and erases traces of the malware from the file system after execution to hinder forensic recovery.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — self-deletion after in-memory load leaves little discrete signal; hunt via memory-resident/fileless detection and short-lived-file telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: Captured keystroke data is staged locally in %TEMP% (wlg.dat / AdobeARM.log / AdobeARMM.log) and, once a log exceeds ~3,000 bytes, queued for upload; log files are renamed LOG_(UserName)_[timestamp] prior to exfiltration.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — growth of specific %TEMP% log files and their rename to a LOG_username_timestamp pattern before egress are detectable via file-write and file-rename telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: Beyond keystrokes, actors steal documents from compromised systems — e.g. genuine files harvested from an impersonated engineer's computer were reused as lures — supporting espionage collection on victim endpoints.
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — local document collection is common; suspicious mainly in a backdoor/keylogger process-lineage and staging context

ttps.procedure_description: GHOLE beacons over HTTP to a hard-coded C2 IP using GET requests of the form /index.php?c=<8-byte id>&r=<5-7 byte>&u=1&t=<time>, with variants /index.php?c=%s&r=%lx and /index.php?c=%s&r=%x usable as network IOCs.
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — the distinctive /index.php?c=&r=&u=&t= URI pattern to hard-coded C2 IPs is a strong network-detection/IDS signature via proxy and TLS/HTTP metadata

ttps.procedure_description: GHOLE uses a hard-coded 256-byte (2,048-bit) symmetric key to encrypt its command-and-control network communications.
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — custom-encrypted C2 defeats content inspection but is detectable via the embedded key/algorithm in samples and via beacon-timing/destination analytics

ttps.procedure_description: Actors retrieve secondary payloads/decoys from attacker-controlled cloud (OneDrive) after initial link click; some keylogger versions removed the built-in uploader in favor of a separately delivered companion binary (wsnd.exe) placed in the same folder.
observed_tooling: Microsoft OneDrive (payload hosting)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — download of executables from cloud storage followed by execution, and appearance of companion binaries (wsnd.exe) alongside the keylogger, are detectable via proxy + file-creation telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: GHOLE is a modified Core Impact Pro agent providing remote control/backdoor access to infected hosts; a fake Trend Micro HouseCall installer establishes a further backdoor connection to C2 84.11.146.62.
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
Fake Trend Micro HouseCall installer (HousecallLauncher.exe backdoor installer)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — the modified Core Impact agent and fake-HouseCall installer are detectable via sample signatures/hashes and their fixed C2 destinations, though a custom agent is less name-recognizable than commodity RMM

ttps.procedure_description: GHOLE exfiltrates collected data to its operators over its HTTP/encrypted C2 channel to hard-coded C2 IP addresses (e.g. 83.170.33.60).
observed_tooling: GHOLE / Gholee (BKDR_GHOLE / TROJ_GHOLE, backdoor; modified Core Impact agent)
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — outbound data to the fixed C2 IPs correlated with the GHOLE URI pattern is detectable at the network egress, but volume alone is subtle

ttps.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
ttps.procedure_description: The CWoolger keylogger exfiltrates staged keystroke logs over FTP using hard-coded credentials to attacker FTP servers (107.6.172.54/woolen/, earlier 107.6.181.116), calling an uploadToCnC function once a log exceeds ~3,000 bytes.
observed_tooling: CWoolger / TSPY_WOOLERG (keylogger, aka Woolen-Goldfish keylogger)
FTP (hard-coded credentials for keylog exfiltration)
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — outbound FTP from a workstation to the hard-coded exfil IPs, uploading LOG_username_timestamp files to a /woolen/ path, is a strong network-detection opportunity via flow/proxy logging and destination-IP blocklists

detection_signals: Microsoft Office application (excel/powerpnt/winword) spawning a script or dropping/loading a DLL or EXE — GHOLE macro chain (delivery docs detected as X2KM_DROPPR)
Execution of a double-extension file with a document icon (e.g. *.ppt.exe) that drops a benign decoy and a hidden payload
Creation of %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe or NTUSER.dat{GUID}.exe; mutex named 'woolger'; VBScript %TEMP%\wsc.vbs installing persistence
New Startup-folder shortcut named 'WinDefender' (Notepad icon) whose target resides in %TEMP% — CWoolger persistence
Creation/growth of keystroke-log files %TEMP%\wlg.dat, %TEMP%\AdobeARM.log, or %TEMP%\AdobeARMM.log by a non-Adobe process; use of SetWindowsHookExW keyboard hooks from an unsigned %TEMP% binary
Rename of local log files to LOG_(UserName)_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS immediately before an outbound transfer
Outbound FTP uploads to 107.6.172.54 (/woolen/ path) or 107.6.181.116 carrying LOG_* files
HTTP GET requests matching /index.php?c=<8chars>&r=<5-7chars>&u=1&t= (and /index.php?c=%s&r=%lx , /index.php?c=%s&r=%x) to hard-coded C2 IPs — GHOLE beacon
Execution of a file masquerading as Trend Micro HouseCall (HousecallLauncher.exe) beaconing to 84.11.146.62
Presence of any GHOLE/WOOLERG/X2KM_DROPPR sample hash (see iocs.hashes)
Inbound spear-phishing with OneDrive links to executable payloads, or links to look-alike webmail/portal login pages (credential harvesting)
Post-phishing anomalous webmail/portal authentication (impossible travel, new device) consistent with harvested-credential reuse
notes: Primary sources are three peer-corroborated 2015 vendor reports with concrete IOC appendices (Trend Micro Operation Woolen-GoldFish; Trend Micro The Spy Kittens Are Back / Rocket Kitten 2; ClearSky Thamar Reservoir) plus Check Point 'Rocket Kitten: A Campaign With 9 Lives', enriched by MITRE ATT&CK Ajax Security Team G0130 (the cluster MITRE uses for Rocket Kitten). Report confidence is 'high' on the technical TTPs/IOCs (multiple independent primary sources with raw hashes/IPs); actor attribution to an IRGC-aligned Iran-nexus group is set to 'medium-high' per tasking, honestly reflecting the convergence-based (not smoking-gun) case and the deliberate note that Rocket Kitten overlaps with Ajax/Flying Kitten/Saffron Rose and is DISTINCT from Charming Kitten. actor.mitre_id intentionally left empty per spec (public MITRE id G0130 cited only in source/aliases/notes; the task-supplied 'G0048' is INCORRECT — in this environment and public MITRE G0048 = RTM, an unrelated Russian banking-crime group — so it was not used). ATT&CK normalization: this env has no 'defense-evasion' tactic, so evasion techniques use slug 'stealth'; File Deletion (T1070.004) placed under 'defense-impairment' per env tactic conventions; every technique_id was validated as a key in the bundled attack_dump.json (697 techniques) before inclusion — zero invalid IDs, no substitutions were required. STRONGEST DETECTION SURFACE (detect candidates, medium/high): T1204.002 Office-spawns-dropper macro chain, T1137.001/T1059.005 VBA+wsc.vbs, T1547.001/T1547.009 'WinDefender' Startup .lnk to %TEMP%\NTSuser.exe (mutex 'woolger'), T1056.001 keylog to wlg.dat/AdobeARM.log, T1071.001 GHOLE /index.php?c=&r=&u=&t= beacon, T1048.003 FTP keylog exfil to 107.6.172.54//woolen//, T1219 GHOLE/fake-HouseCall backdoors, sample hashes. HUNT-leaning (low, off-victim/social): T1589/T1591 recon, T1585.001/.002/T1586.002 personas & impersonation, T1583.001/.006/T1608.001/T1587.001/T1588.002 infra & tooling, T1566.003 social-platform delivery, T1598.003/T1056.003 fake-login credential harvesting, T1070.004 self-deletion. IOC scope decisions: iocs.domains left EMPTY deliberately — the Woolen-Goldfish/Spy Kittens reports hard-code C2 as IP addresses (no C2 domains), and the Check Point/ClearSky phishing-domain lists could not be extracted verbatim from their PDFs in this session, so no domain is asserted rather than risk a hallucinated/legit-CDN value; the free Iranian scanner av.zerodays.ir and old WHOIS-pivot domains (livenetsat.com, joinebiz.com) are actor-adjacent attribution artifacts, NOT C2, and are intentionally excluded from iocs. Hashes are SHA1 taken verbatim from the Trend Micro appendices (GHOLE/BKDR_GHOLE/TROJ_GHOLE backdoors, X2KM_DROPPR macro droppers, TSPY_WOOLERG/CWoolger keylogger variants, fake HouseCall installer af364ff5..., NTUSER.dat{GUID}.exe dropper 64ba130e..., and companion FILE2 457f54e9...). CVEs empty: Rocket Kitten relied on social-engineering/macro user-execution, not exploited CVEs, in the cited reporting.
